Subject: Hosted API pricing — bucketed commit / per-token tiers

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the platform looks promising for our conversational care workflows. Were evaluating expected usage for year 1 and want to propose a committed, bucketed pricing structure rather than the public rate card. Quick background:

- Expected consumption: ~18B tokens in year 1, ramping to 45B in year 2 (mostly chat generation).
- We'd like monthly billing, but are open to quarterly commit invoicing if that helps with discounting.
- Main ask: a per-token volume discount schedule (buckets) that gives predictability for unit economics and a committed floor.

Can your team share what flexibility you have vs the standard rate card? Also, any constraints on minimum commit, billing cadence, and approval path for custom pricing exceptions? Wed like a rough indicative term sheet to take to procurement.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a brief call if that helps.

Best,
Emily
Head of Platform Partnerships
Brightline Health

Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the projection. Appreciate the context.

Short answer: we can do bucketed commit pricing with per-token discounts, and we frequently handle monthly or quarterly billing depending on the customer. There are two internal levers that matter for approvals:

1) Depth of discount vs public rate card (discounts >25% need VP approval).
2) Whether the commit is non-refundable (we can offer true committed spend or a partially refundable structure).

Ill pull together an initial indicative model (attached) and loop in pricing + legal. Karthik, Marcus — can you weigh in on the buckets we should propose for Brightline given the projected 18B first-year baseline? Im including the projection file and a working pricing_model.xlsx in this thread.

Emily — will follow up with a short term sheet and proposed buckets by tomorrow. If procurement wants net-30 billing, flag that now.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — bucketed commit / per-token tiers

Following up with a suggested structure for Brightline that balances predictability and upside:

Proposed buckets (monthly equivalent):
- Tier A: 0 - 500M tokens/month => list rate (no discount)
- Tier B: 500M - 2.5B tokens/month => 12% off per-token rate
- Tier C: 2.5B - 6B tokens/month => 20% off per-token rate
- Tier D: >6B tokens/month => 30% off per-token rate (requires VP approval)

Commit options:
- Option 1: Annual committed spend of $XXXk (monthly true-ups) — gives applied discounts by bucket with quarterly reconciliations.
- Option 2: Quarterly committed invoicing with a refundable overage credit — higher discount floor (~3-5% better) but adds finance complexity.

Notes/assumptions:
- These discounts assume standard quantization profiles; deeper quantization (Q4x) may unlock smaller unit cost and could be shared with customer for additional savings.
- Any discount >25% triggers a formal pricing exception and requires VP signoff + Legal redlines.

Ive attached a draft SOW template (Brightline_SOW_v2.pdf) with the billing cadence language wed use. Marcus — please add SE notes on expected latency/throughput sizing for a 6B token/month slice.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts

Looping in revenue ops questions before we proceed with any formal pricing exception:

- Billing cadence: If we do monthly true-ups, we need to confirm whether net-30 or net-45 is acceptable to Brightline. Net-45 increases our working capital exposure.
- Minimum commit: Clarify whether Brightline expects a hard annual minimum or a soft monthly floor with true-ups.
- Credit / Refund policy: For Option 2 (quarterly refundable model) we need the language around how refundable credits are earned and applied.

Also — per internal policy, any pricing that results in realized revenue < 75% of list over the first 6 months requires VP of Revenue approval. Karthik, can you estimate the expected realized revenue % under your proposed Option 1? If it drops below that threshold we should prepare an approval memo.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
